body.en: Steps: select a SEBI-registered broker (stockbroker); open a *trading* account with the broker and a demat account with a depository participant (DP), completing KYC with PAN and bank details; place an order (buy or sell, quantity, market order or limit price) online or through the broker; the order is matched electronically on the exchange's screen-based system and executed; the broker issues a contract note giving the details of the trade; and the trade is settled: money is paid and shares are delivered through the clearing corporation.

body.en: A market order buys or sells at the best available price at once; a limit order is executed only at the price set or better; a stop-loss order sells automatically if the price falls to a set level, limiting the loss. Every trade carries *charges*: brokerage, securities transaction tax (STT), exchange transaction charges, SEBI fees, stamp duty and GST on services. The investor's gain on a trade is the change in price times the quantity, minus these charges, plus any dividend received.

say.en: Asha buys 100 shares at 250 rupees and sells them at 280, rupees receiving a dividend of 5 rupees a share in between. Charges total 150 rupees. Find her net gain.
Capital gain equals 280 minus 250 times 100 equals 3,000 rupees.
Dividend equals 5 times 100 equals 500 rupees.
Total before charges equals 3,500 rupees.
Net gain equals 3,500 rupees minus 150 rupees equals 3,350 rupees.
So the answer is 3,350 rupees.
